data.forecast: Open-Meteo Previous Runs API, day-ahead (previous_day1) best-match forecast
data.observed: ERA5 reanalysis (Open-Meteo Historical Weather API): a model reconstruction, not station measurements

solar.units: W/m2 (hourly, daylight hours); daily energy in kWh/m2

backtest.note: Demand from climatology for each date; solar from the archived day-ahead forecast (raw) or the ML curves (ml); both schedules replayed against ERA5 solar with the feeder's grid backup.

limitations: Trained on 20 months; forecast errors differ between years, so the cautious curve is somewhat optimistic on the held-out year (see belowCautious against its 10% target).
An upper (P90) band was tested and is not shipped: it was badly under-calibrated on the held-out year.

Rain fell on 15% of held-out days against 26% in training; in that drier year the rain model's mid-range probabilities were too high (see the reliability table), although it still beat the forecast's yes/no on every score.
Day-ahead forecasts (24 h+ lead) are used for training; same-day plans use fresher forecasts, so the corrections are, if anything, conservative for them.
ERA5 is the reference for 'what happened'; it has its own errors against ground stations.
